extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of philosophy of biology / general readers interested in Bergson's theory of evolution
extracted.subtask_description: A conceptual/theoretical treatment of the movement of life and evolutionary divergence, distinguishing plants and animals by their tendencies and proposing methodological rules for interpreting evolutionary history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation is necessary but not the directing cause
rubrics_metrics.description: Adaptation to environment is a necessary condition for survival, but outer circumstances are not the directing causes of evolution; adaptation explains local sinuosities of the movement but not its general directions or the movement itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: some taxa (Foraminifera, Lingulae) show long-term stasis despite environmental upheavals. Analogy: a road adapts to hills (accidents of the ground) but the road is not caused by the hills; the road aims at the town. Thus adaptation furnishes indispensable conditions (the soil) but is not the origin of the evolutionary direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject finalism: evolution is not the realization of a pre-given plan
rubrics_metrics.description: If life realized a plan, harmony would increase and the future would be conceptually sketched from the present; instead, evolution continually creates new forms and ideas, so its future overflows the present and cannot be formulated beforehand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalism implies a single coherent idea guiding development; Bergson argues observation shows divergence, incompatibilities and increasing discord between species, contradicting the expectations of a plan-driven process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of life arises from an initial impetus rather than teleology
rubrics_metrics.description: The unity of life is derived from a vis a tergo—an initial internal push that drives life forward—rather than from an attraction toward a final goal; this impetus splits and generates divergent, often incompatible manifestations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences: harmony is found retrospectively (behind), not prospectively (in front). The impulse can produce both progress along a few main lines and many blind alleys, arrests, and retrogressions elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method: follow main lines of evolution rather than contested genealogical details
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the full history of organized life is not known and proposed genealogies are often variable and debatable, one should concentrate on the principal directions of evolutionary movement (the main lines) to avoid error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical note: focus on the large-scale directions (especially the line leading to man) rather than attempting definitive species-by-species genealogies; allowing for accidents and incoherence and identifying centers where incoherence crystallizes will clarify the main directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define biological groups by tendency rather than possession of static characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Groups (e.g., plant vs animal) should be defined not by possession of particular static attributes but by their tendency to emphasize certain characters as they evolve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation: individual manifestations often show rudimentary characters of others; what matters is the direction a group tends to develop indefinitely. This dynamic definition tolerates exceptions while capturing divergent developmental trajectories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish plants and animals by method of alimentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Vegetables (plants) manufacture organic matter directly from air, water and soil (mineral inputs), while animals cannot assimilate these elements directly and must obtain fixed organic substances from plants or other animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions exist (insectivorous plants, fungi feeding like animals), so this is not a rigid static diagnostic; rather it signals divergent evolutionary directions tied to nutrition and subsequent developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish plants and animals by mobility versus fixity
rubrics_metrics.description: Animals have evolved toward mobility in space (locomotion, sense-organs, nervous coordination) while plants have trended toward fixity and sedentary habits due to their capacity to draw mineral elements from surroundings without moving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Again exceptions occur (movements in plants, sessile animals/parasites). The balance of tendencies (mobility vs fixity) rather than absolute presence/absence is diagnostic: mobility favors animal evolution, fixity favors vegetable evolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish by degree of consciousness tied to mobility
rubrics_metrics.description: Consciousness correlates with freedom of movement: the more an organism can move freely and choose among movements, the greater the consciousness; plants exhibit 'consciousness asleep' whereas animals tend toward awakened sensibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The nervous system is a canalized division of labor that intensifies and specifies this rudimentary activity; lack of a brain does not imply absence of consciousness in simpler organisms. Vegetative 'impressionability' (e.g., chlorophyl reaction to light) plays an analogous but distinct role in plants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nervous system as division of labor, not originator of function
rubrics_metrics.description: The nervous system arises from division of labor and does not create consciousness or movement, but brings rudimentary, diffused activity to higher degrees of intensity and precision (reflex and voluntary forms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication: absence of nervous elements does not imply absence of the functions they later canalize; simpler organisms may possess vague, undecided reactions that are proto-conscious or proto-motor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy strategy as a criterion: accumulation vs expenditure
rubrics_metrics.description: A fundamental divergence is whether life tends to accumulate solar energy into potential chemical reservoirs (plants) or to expend stored energy discontinuously in locomotion and activity (animals); this difference shapes evolutionary direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustration: plants manufacture complex molecules that store solar energy; animals use such reservoirs as 'explosives' to power movement. Primitive organisms may have combined both tendencies (e.g., Euglena).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow for accident and incoherence when interpreting evolution
rubrics_metrics.description: One must make a liberal allowance for accident and recognize that nature is not wholly coherent; not everything in nature fits a unified plan, so identify centers where incoherence crystallizes to clarify main directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical consequence: rejecting an assumption of total coherence prevents forcing disparate facts into a single scheme and helps isolate principal evolutionary lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evolution proceeds by dissociation rather than association
rubrics_metrics.description: Evolution is characterized by dissociation — splitting of original tendencies into divergent directions — rather than by association and convergence; this yields complementary but often antagonistic series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequently, apparent harmony between divergent forms stems from their common origin, not from subsequent reciprocal adaptation; division of labor in the usual sense implies association, whereas Bergson's dissociation yields divergence of effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law of preservation within specialization
rubrics_metrics.description: When a tendency splits during development, each arising special tendency attempts to preserve and develop everything in the primitive tendency that is not incompatible with the role for which it becomes specialized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains recurring analogies across independent evolutionary lines (e.g., sexual generation appearing in both kingdoms) and why residual recollections of the primitive tendency remain active within specialized branches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize principal directions leading to man for anthropological perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: In studying evolution with respect to the human place in nature, give special attention to the principal direction(s) of evolution which culminate in man while still considering other divergent lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a methodological priority rather than an exclusion: while following various directions, keep the relation of man to the animal kingdom as a central concern.
